exact_supplier_excerpts.excerpt: Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded closed convex set with nonempty interior, and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be an open convex set such that $\operatorname{int}(K)\subseteq U$ and $K\subseteq\overline U$. If a decision set is lower-dimensional in an ambient Euclidean space, take $\mathbb R^d$ to be orthonormal affine coordinates on its affine hull (the smallest affine subspace containing it); thus interior, gradients, Hessians, and norms are relative to that affine hull. A **mirror regularizer** on $(K,U)$ is a real-valued function $R$ on $K\cup U$ that is continuous on $K$, twice continuously differentiable on $U$, agrees on $K\cap U$, and has symmetric positive-definite Hessian $H_R(z):=\nabla^2R(z)$ for every $z\in U$. We call $R$ $m$-strongly convex on $K$ in the Euclidean norm if, for some $m>0$, all $x,y\in K$ and $\lambda\in[0,1]$ satisfy $$R((1-\lambda)x+\lambda y)\le (1-\lambda)R(x)+\lambda R(y)-\frac m2\lambda(1-\lambda)\|x-y\|_2^2.$$ For $x\in K\cup U$ and $y\in U$, the **Bregman divergence** generated by $R$ is $$B_R(x\|y):=R(x)-R(y)-\langle\nabla R(y),x-y\rangle.$$ For $z\in U$ and vectors $v,h\in\mathbb R^d$, define the squared **local primal norm** and **local dual norm** by $$\|v\|_z^2:=v^\top H_R(z)v,\qquad \|h\|_{*,z}^2:=h^\top H_R(z)^{-1}h.$$

exact_supplier_excerpts.excerpt: Fix a positive integer horizon $T$, a nonempty action set $K$, and, when choices or the environment are randomized, a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$. An online decision protocol has rounds $t=1,\ldots,T$. Before round $t$, the learner has the history $h_{t-1}$ consisting of its earlier choices and all feedback and loss information revealed in earlier rounds. It chooses $x_t\in K$ using only $h_{t-1}$ and any learner-private randomization available by that time. In a randomized protocol, $X_t$ is a measurable random element of $K$, meaning a measurable map from $(\Omega,\mathcal F)$ into $K$ equipped with its declared measurable structure. The environment supplies a real-valued loss function $f_t:K\to\mathbb R$; it may have fixed $f_t$ before the choice or choose it after the choice, as specified by the environment model, but the learner does not observe $f_t$ before choosing $x_t$. The learner incurs loss $f_t(x_t)$ and then receives feedback about round $t$ according to the feedback model. The history $h_t$ adds $x_t$, the feedback received, and any part of $f_t$ explicitly revealed in round $t$. No convexity, boundedness, or regret guarantee is part of this protocol definition.

exact_supplier_excerpts.excerpt: Let $d\ge1$ be an integer and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, bounded, closed, and convex; let $x_1\in K$, let $T\ge1$ be an integer, and fix a step size $\eta>0$. At round $t$, play $x_t$, then receive the full current loss information and its prescribed gradient vector $g_t\in\mathbb R^d$. Set $G_0=0$ and $$G_t=G_{t-1}+g_tg_t^\top=\sum_{s=1}^t g_sg_s^\top.$$ The accumulated matrix $G_t$ is symmetric and positive semidefinite because $v^\top G_tv=\sum_{s=1}^t(g_s^\top v)^2\ge0$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^d$. Choose either the **full-matrix scale** $H_t=G_t^{1/2}$, the unique positive-semidefinite square root, or the **diagonal scale** $H_t=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{(G_t)_{11}},\ldots,\sqrt{(G_t)_{dd}})$. Define $H_t^\dagger$ to be the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse and update $$y_{t+1}=x_t-\eta H_t^\dagger g_t,\qquad x_{t+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in K}(x-y_{t+1})^\top H_t(x-y_{t+1}).$$ A minimizer exists; if it is not unique, select any minimizer. Return $x_1,\ldots,x_T$. The matrix seminorm notation in the objective means $\|v\|_{H_t}^2=v^\top H_tv$. The diagonal scale here is formed by taking each diagonal entry of $G_t$ and then its scalar square root; in general it is not $\operatorname{diag}(G_t^{1/2})$. This is an update definition only and asserts no regret bound.

If a decision set is lower-dimensional in an ambient Euclidean space, take $\mathbb R^d$ to be orthonormal affine coordinates on its affine hull (the smallest affine subspace containing it); thus interior, gradients, Hessians, and norms are relative to that affine hull. A **mirror regularizer** on $(K,U)$ is a real-valued function $R$ on $K\cup U$ that is continuous on $K$, twice continuously differentiable on $U$, agrees on $K\cap U$, and has symmetric positive-definite Hessian $H_R(z):=\nabla^2R(z)$ for every $z\in U$. We call $R$ $m$-strongly convex on $K$ in the Euclidean norm if, for some $m>0$, all $x,y\in K$ and $\lambda\in[0,1]$ satisfy $$R((1-\lambda)x+\lambda y)\le (1-\lambda)R(x)+\lambda R(y)-\frac m2\lambda(1-\lambda)\|x-y\|_2^2.$$ For $x\in K\cup U$ and $y\in U$, the **Bregman divergence** generated by $R$ is $$B_R(x\|y):=R(x)-R(y)-\langle\nabla R(y),x-y\rangle.$$ For $z\in U$ and vectors $v,h\in\mathbb R^d$, define the squared **local primal norm** and **local dual norm** by $$\|v\|_z^2:=v^\top H_R(z)v,\qquad \|h\|_{*,z}^2:=h^\top H_R(z)^{-1}h.$$

exact_supplier_excerpts.excerpt: Let $N,T\ge1$ be integers, let $[N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ be the expert set, and let $\epsilon>0$. At each round $t=1,\ldots,T$, a finite loss vector $\ell_t=(\ell_t(1),\ldots,\ell_t(N))\in[0,\infty)^N$ is revealed after the learner's choice. Initialize $W_1(i)=1$ for every $i\in[N]$. At round $t$, set $$x_t(i):=\frac{W_t(i)}{\sum_{j=1}^{N}W_t(j)},\qquad i\in[N],$$ draw a measurable expert choice $I_t\in[N]$ with $\mathbb P(I_t=i)=x_t(i)$, and play $I_t$. After observing the whole vector $\ell_t$, update $$W_{t+1}(i):=W_t(i)\exp(-\epsilon\ell_t(i)),\qquad i\in[N].$$ The output is the distributions $x_1,\ldots,x_T$, the sampled choices $I_1,\ldots,I_T$, and the final weights. Every factor $\exp(-\epsilon\ell_t(i))$ is a positive finite real; from the positive finite initial weights it follows by induction that every normalizing denominator is positive and finite. The protocol assumes a probability space carrying the stated measurable draws; no probability-space construction is claimed.

exact_supplier_excerpts.excerpt: Let $d,T\ge1$ be integers, let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $D,G\ge0$ be finite real bounds such that $\|u-v\|_2\le D$ for all $u,v\in K$ and $\|g_t\|_2\le G$. Supply an initial point $x_1\in K$. At each round $t=1,\ldots,T$, the learner plays $x_t$ and then receives the full loss function $f_t$ or the prescribed vector $g_t$. The smooth branch takes $f_t:U_t\to\mathbb R$ differentiable and convex on an open convex set $U_t\supseteq K$, with $g_t=\nabla f_t(x_t)$. The nonsmooth branch takes a convex function $f_t:C_t\to\mathbb R$ on a convex set $C_t\supseteq K$ and a supplied $g_t\in\partial f_t(x_t)$, where $\partial f_t(x_t)$ consists of vectors $g$ satisfying $f_t(y)\ge f_t(x_t)+\langle g,y-x_t\rangle$ for every $y\in C_t$; require explicitly that this inequality holds for every $u\in K$. If $D=0$ or $G=0$, set $x_{t+1}=x_t$ at every round. If $D,G>0$, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the metric projection. Set $\eta_t=D/(G\sqrt t)$, put $y_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tg_t$, and set $x_{t+1}=P_K(y_{t+1})$, the unique point of $K$ minimizing Euclidean distance to $y_{t+1}$. Return the decisions $x_1,\ldots,x_T$. For random inputs, assume $x_1$ and each supplied $g_t$ are measurable; the nonexpansive projection map is continuous, so each projected update remains measurable.
